note: Adapted from Maiti 2006; original in English; the measurements in the text are quoted from Kemner (1931) and given alongside Table 13, the two differing slightly in head width (text 0.99—1.00, Table 13 0.90—1.00) and both are transcribed; in Table 13 the head height row is a single value in the extracted text and cannot be matched to the three columns, so it is not recorded.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head strongly narrowed anteriorly, almost to half the length of the mandibles, usually with 2 setae at the tip; mandibles long and slender; antennae short, scarcely reaching the tip of the mandibles, 13—14-segmented; postmentum almost twice as wide as long. The fontanelle opening faces backwards and is chitinized, and the maximum head width lies posteriorly, which distinguishes the species from the others.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head strongly narrowed anteriorly, the tip almost reaching half the length of the mandibles, usually with 2 setae; mandibles long and slender; antennae short, scarcely reaching the tip of the mandibles, 13—14-segmented: with 13 segments segment 3 large, larger than segments 2 and 4; with 14 segments segment 3 smaller than segment 2 and slightly larger than segment 4. Postmentum almost twice as wide as long; pronotum almost twice as wide as long, posterior margin nearly straight, erect hairs scattered along the margins and on the disc. Measurements (mm, after Kemner 1931): head with mandibles 1.84; head without mandibles 1.09—1.13; head width 0.99—1.00; pronotum width 0.63—0.68; pronotum length 0.31—0.35. Table 13 additionally records: head length to the lateral base of the mandible 1.09—1.13; maximum head width 0.90—1.00; anterior head width 0.58—0.63; head index 0.82—0.90; mandible length 0.74; postmentum midlength 0.70, maximum width 0.31, waist width 0.21; pronotum length 0.32, width 0.65; antennae 13-segmented.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Distribution: Amboina, Asia, and also recorded from South Pacific islands (Bees, 1970). The depository of the type specimens is unknown. The alate and worker have not been described.
